scams.name: Port Gruž Cruise-Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: A taxi rank positioned immediately outside Port Gruž cruise terminal funnels disembarking passengers into unmetered cars at flat €40–80 fares for Old Town runs that should cost €12–20 metered. A British cruise passenger on Tripadvisor (Jun 7, 2024) was charged €55 for a 15-minute Gruž-to-Old Town ride where Uber was quoting €12. The Dubrovnik Times (Aug 9, 2025) reported an unlicensed driver hid his plates with garbage bags to enter Dubrovnik's Special Traffic Management Zone; the mayor proposed amending the Road Transport Act in Sep 2025. Transport Minister Oleg Butković announced on Nova TV Dnevnik (Aug 28, 2025) that fare caps would be reintroduced in response to Split and Dubrovnik cases. Cruise Critic's 'Dubrovnik late afternoon Taxi scams' thread documents the return-to-ship window specifically.
scams.avoidance: Open Uber or Bolt before leaving the ship — both operate legally in Dubrovnik and show the full fare up front (the US State Department Croatia advisory explicitly recommends them). Take Libertas bus 1A or 1B from Gruž to Pile Gate for €2, or the cruise shuttle if your line offers one. Photograph the taxi's plate, the driver's ID, and the meter before loading luggage. Pay by card with a receipt showing the company's business registration number; refuse cash-only drivers. Report overcharges to 112 (EU emergency) or the Dubrovnik-Neretva Police on +385 20 443 333 within 48 hours. Dubrovnik Tourist Board at Brsalje 5, +385 20 312 011, handles Tourism Quality Service complaints.
scams.location: Port Gruž cruise terminal (Obala Ivana Pavla II), especially the right-hand taxi rank outside the arrivals gate; Pile Gate taxi stand on Branitelja Dubrovnika; Ploče Gate at the end of Frana Supila; Dubrovnik airport (DBV) at Čilipi

scams.name: Old Town Menu Bait-and-Switch
scams.description: Old Town restaurants on Stradun, Prijeko and Od Puča post the cheapest item on a chalkboard outside, then hand you a menu 2–3× more expensive once you are seated. Anchor prices inside the walls: €5 for a scoop of gelato, €25+ for a seafood pasta, €6 for a coffee on the Stradun (Croatia Travel Facebook group, 2024 Viralsnare investigation). A 2024 Tripadvisor thread walks through the mechanic at Korta Bistro & Wine Bar just off Stradun. The Medium piece 'The Terrible Story Of How I Got Scammed In Dubrovnik' documents 70 kuna (~€9.30) for a single juice with menu-swap photos. Community reports summarize the post-euro picture. Three moves: different chalkboard vs table menu; seafood 'market price by the kilogram' with no weight disclosed (whole sea bass €60–90); and cover charges (coperto) of €3–5 per person in small type at the bottom of the bill.
scams.avoidance: Eat outside the walls — Lapad, Gruž, Ploče — where prices are half and the food is often better. Ask for the English menu with printed prices before you order; photograph the chalkboard menu in the alley next to your table number. For seafood, always confirm price per kilogram and the final total in euros before the fish goes to the grill. Pay by card for chargeback recourse. For disputes, call the Croatian Ministry of Finance consumer hotline 072 213 213, Dubrovnik-Neretva Police on 112 or +385 20 443 333, and Dubrovnik Tourist Board on +385 20 312 011.
scams.location: Stradun (Placa) and its side-alleys inside the walls — especially Prijeko, Od Puča, and the cluster around Pile Gate; Ploče Gate promenade between Revelin and Banje Beach; restaurant terraces on Buža Gate overlooking the sea

scams.name: Fake Apartment & Booking.com Reservation Hijack
scams.description: A 26-year-old Slovak tourist lost €1,050 in March 2025 to a fake Dubrovnik rental advertised on what looked like a legitimate booking site (Dubrovnik Times, Mar 18, 2025). The Polish embassy in Zagreb has publicly warned its citizens about scammers publishing the same Dubrovnik apartment under several names and prices on Booking.com to trigger overbookings (TVP World, 2024). The BBC's Nov 2024 'reservation hijacking' story documents the data-breach pattern: leaked guest bookings sent to criminals who WhatsApp the target impersonating the hotel and demand a 'card verification' payment. Three mechanic versions: cloned-listing (scammer copies a real apartment to Instagram/Marketplace or phishing domain, takes €500–1,500 SEPA transfer and disappears); reservation-hijack (WhatsApp credential phish after legitimate Booking.com booking); and overbooking (same apartment listed three or four times on Booking.com at different prices, first tourist through the door keeps it). Slobodna Dalmacija's Neum fake-villa exposé shows the pattern targets the broader Dalmatian coast.
scams.avoidance: Book only through the official Booking.com, Airbnb, or Vrbo app — never through an email link — and ignore any request for card verification or payment outside the platform, regardless of the logo on the message. Pay only on arrival, keys in hand. Cross-check apartment addresses in the Croatian eVisitor tourism registry and host names at sudreg.pravosudje.hr (both free). Use a credit card with chargeback rights; never pay by SEPA before arrival. For losses, call Dubrovnik-Neretva Police on +385 20 443 333, your card fraud line within 30 days, and Croatian Ombudsman +385 1 49 21 837. US Embassy Zagreb +385 1 661 2200, UK Embassy Zagreb +385 1 6009 100 for emergency accommodation referrals.
scams.location: Listings claiming Old Town, Lapad, Babin Kuk, or Gruž addresses; phishing messages appearing to come from Booking.com, Airbnb, or an apartment owner after a legitimate booking; WhatsApp and email follow-ups from fake 'hosts'

scams.name: City Walls & Dubrovnik Pass Fake-Ticket Resellers
scams.description: The official Dubrovnik City Walls ticket is €35 adults in 2025 (or bundled into the €40 Dubrovnik Pass from dubrovnikpass.com), but third-party resellers sell the same ticket at €45–70 with a 'skip-the-line' label that does not skip anything — and a parallel ecosystem of phishing websites charges your card and emails an unusable voucher. A canonical Tripadvisor review ('SCAM — use official site Dubrovnik Pass,' on Gulliver Travel) records €50 per person; a Viator 'Skip-the-Line Dubrovnik Cable Car' review logs €92 vs €52 at the counter. The Srđ Cable Car official return ticket is €27 at the Petra Krešimira IV lower terminus. Three mechanic versions: phishing domains like 'dubrovnikcitywalls.com' that take card and email a QR that fails at Pile Gate; legitimate-but-marked-up OTA listings at 20–100% above counter; and street touts at Pile and Brsalje selling already-used tickets or laminated cards the gate does not recognize.
scams.avoidance: Buy City Walls and Old Town monument tickets at dubrovnikpass.com (Dubrovnik Tourist Board's own portal) or at the Pile Gate, Ploče Gate, or St. John's Fort ticket booths on the day — there is no meaningful 'skip-the-line' option. Buy Srđ Cable Car tickets at dubrovnikcablecar.com or the Petra Krešimira IV lower terminus counter. Refuse street touts — Croatian law requires licensed tour operators to wear a visible Ministry of Tourism badge with a license number. For phishing losses, call your card issuer's 24-hour fraud line, file at Dubrovnik-Neretva Police on +385 20 443 333, and call the Croatian Ministry of Finance consumer hotline 072 213 213.
scams.location: Pile Gate ticket booth on Placa; Ploče Gate and St. John's Fort secondary entrances; street touts around Pile and Brsalje; third-party websites and Google ads advertising 'skip-the-line Dubrovnik City Walls tickets'

scams.name: Fake-QR-Code Parking Meter
scams.description: In July 2025, Dubrovnik police discovered scammers had pasted stickers with fake QR codes over legitimate codes on parking meters across the city. Tourists scanning them were routed to a phishing page that captured card details instead of paying for parking; the City of Dubrovnik peeled dozens of stickers off, per community reports. Drivers who thought they had 'paid' still got tickets while losing card numbers, expiry, CVV, and 3-D Secure codes. An older Tripadvisor 'Be Aware of Parking Scam' thread from the Pile / cable-car lower-terminus car park documents an adjacent pattern — fake high-vis 'attendants' demanding cash for 'parking' on streets where parking is actually metered. Separately, MSN documents a Dalmatian-coast SMS parking-phishing variant in which tourists receive a 'unpaid ticket' text with a payment link after the fact.
scams.avoidance: Pay Dubrovnik parking only via the official Sanitat payDo+ app (Apple App Store / Google Play) or coin/card directly at the meter's physical interface — do not scan roadside QR codes unless you have verified the URL against the printed domain on the meter. Verify any URL shows sanitat.hr or dubrovnik.hr before entering card details. If you already entered details into a suspect QR site, block your card immediately with your issuer and call Dubrovnik-Neretva Police +385 20 443 333. Legitimate Dubrovnik tickets are paper on the windscreen — ignore post-trip SMS/WhatsApp/email 'unpaid parking ticket' messages, which are phishing. Dubrovnik Tourist Board at Brsalje 5, +385 20 312 011.
scams.location: Sanita Park and the Lapad parking zones; parking meters along Ante Starčevića, Iva Vojnovića, Frana Supila; cruise-port adjacent meters on Obala Ivana Pavla II in Gruž; street-side meters near Ploče Gate and the back of the cable-car lower terminus

scams.name: Unlicensed Elafiti & Game of Thrones Tour Operator
scams.description: 'Private' Elafiti boat tours advertised at €400 turn into shared tours with a curtain at the dock, unlicensed skippers offer 'Game of Thrones island hopping' without Croatian maritime insurance, and firsthand Tripadvisor reports document repeated no-show bookings. Three canonical firsthand case files: 'AVOID TRITON. SCAM' on Dubrovnik Boat Excursions (Elafiti private-to-shared switch); 'Super Tours: Tourist scam and overpriced' (Pile Gate GoT island tours); 'Mala Mara: THIS IS A FRAUDULENT BUSINESS AND A SCAM' (Aug 8, 2025 no-show with disputed refund). The Gari Transfer operator guide codifies the three moves: 'private boat = shared with a curtain,' unlicensed boat without safety certification, and bait-and-switch pricing (€400 becomes €550 at the dock). Ministry of Tourism requires licensed tour guides to wear a numbered badge; Pile Gate touts in branded T-shirts are reliably unlicensed.
scams.avoidance: Book island tours through Krilo, Jadrolinija, Dubrovnik Boat Trips (dubrovnikboattrips.com), or OTAs with 1,000+ reviews (GetYourGuide's Elaphite Island Cruise has 4,570+ reviews). For Game of Thrones tours, only book guides displaying a Ministry of Tourism badge with license number — the Dubrovnik Tourist Guides Association at Brsalje 5 (+385 20 312 011) keeps the list. Check VAT number and tax-registered receipt before paying. Never pay more than 30% up front; pay the remainder by card on arrival. For disputes, call the Harbour Master's Office +385 20 418 988 and Dubrovnik-Neretva Police +385 20 443 333.
scams.location: Gruž (Port of Dubrovnik) booking kiosks and walk-up sellers along Obala Ivana Pavla II; the Old Port (Porporela) wooden jetties below St. John's Fort; Pile Gate Game-of-Thrones tour assembly points; Lapad Bay taxi boats; Old Town Mala Braća-square meeting points

scams.name: Stradun Currency Exchange & Euronet ATM Markup
scams.description: Since Croatia adopted the euro on January 1, 2023, currency exchange has become a smaller problem but ATM dynamic-currency-conversion (DCC) markups at independent Euronet machines have filled the gap. Community reports describe Euronet as 'rip-off' and 'scam machines' offering exchange rates 20–25% worse than major Croatian banks; the Adriatic 'is full of nobody's ATMs with brutal [fees]' per a 2025 community report. Paul Bradbury's widely-shared 2024 Facebook post estimates Euronet commissions at 20–25%. The Dubrovnik Times reports EU payment fraud up 43% in 2024 (European Banking Authority). The Split Tourist Board's own article documents tourists receiving 610 kuna for €100 at a booth instead of the legitimate 730–740. Two mechanics: ATM DCC (Euronet/Cashzone/Your Cash defaults the 'accept conversion' button 5–15% worse than your bank rate, plus €4–8 withdrawal fees); and booth exchange with hidden commission of up to 15% in small print.
scams.avoidance: Use only ATMs on the outer wall of a named Croatian bank — Zagrebačka Banka on Stradun, Privredna Banka at Pile Gate, Erste on Obala Stjepana Radića in Gruž, OTP near Ploče. Always decline DCC; choose 'Pay in EUR' / 'Charge without conversion.' Your home bank converts at a far better rate. Withdraw larger amounts less often to minimise per-transaction fees. For manual exchange use a named Croatian-bank branch rather than a street booth. For card fraud call your issuer first, then +385 20 443 333 (Police), +385 1 49 21 837 (Ombudsman), and 072 213 213 (Ministry of Finance consumer hotline).
scams.location: Euronet ATMs clustered along Stradun, Pile Gate, Gruž port, and the Dubrovnik airport arrivals hall; private exchange offices (mjenjačnice) on Stradun and around Ploče Gate; seasonal exchange stalls in Gruž and Lapad

scams.name: Stradun & City Walls Pickpocket Window
scams.description: Pickpocketing inside the walls is concentrated in two predictable compressions — Pile Gate and the viewpoint benches on the City Walls during the mid-day cruise-ship wave. The UK FCDO Croatia safety advisory (2025) explicitly names Split and Dubrovnik as places where 'pickpockets operate in tourist areas.' The Bookiscout Dubrovnik Safety Guide 2026 pins the hottest window: 'Stradun (Placa)... especially from 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM.' Three architectural hotspots: Pile Gate is a single stone arch about three metres wide channelling the entire cruise-ship tide onto Stradun; the City Walls circuit is 1.94 km with viewpoint benches at Minčeta Tower and St. John's Fort where people set bags down to photograph; and the Buža Gate cliff-side bar at sunset with its dark setting and distracting view. The US State Department summarizes: 'Violent crime is rare. Petty crime cases have been reported in densely-populated tourist areas.' Crime tends to be opportunistic rather than organized-group.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags crossbody with the zipper against your chest; keep phone in a zipped front pocket, never a back pocket or the outer mesh pouch of a backpack. At Pile Gate and Ploče Gate, briefly turn your backpack to your front as you pass through the arch. On the City Walls, keep your bag on your lap when you sit on a viewpoint bench. At Buža Gate's cliff bar, keep your phone off the stone bench. Carry only one card and €100–200 in cash; leave the rest in the hotel safe. For thefts, call 112 or 192 (Police) immediately and file at Dubrovnik-Neretva Police on +385 20 443 333. Dubrovnik Tourist Board at Brsalje 5, +385 20 312 011, has a walk-in desk for incident-report referrals.
scams.location: Stradun at peak cruise hours (10:00–14:00 and 17:00–20:00); the Pile Gate bottleneck onto Placa; the Ploče Gate pinch point; the bench-and-viewpoint stops on the City Walls circuit; Buža Gate sea cliffs at sunset; Onofrio's Fountain; Dubrovnik Pass ticket queues
